title: Elide legacy batcher heap, introduce compacting allocator and KV-cache defragmenter
creator: Maya Chen
description: Background: Over multiple iterations the batcher accumulated several legacy heap allocation paths and ad-hoc buffer lifetimes that increase memory fragmentation and amplify tail latency during GC and kernel scheduling. The KV cache has grown hot slabs that are never compacted, causing uneven memory pressure across shards. This ticket consolidates the allocator surface, replaces the largest legacy allocation sites with a compacting allocator shim, and adds an incremental background defragmenter for the KV cache. The overall goal is to reduce p99/p999 token latency during workload surges, lower resident memory growth, and simplify future dependency upgrades by centralizing allocation hooks.
acceptance_criteria: Batcher no longer uses legacy ad-hoc heap paths for ephemeral token buffers (verified by allocator audit and unit tests)
End-to-end p99 for a 2k concurrent chat workload improves by >= 15% in lab harness (measured with runtime-1.21 baseline)
Resident memory growth during long-running loads is reduced by >= 20% on average across KV-sharded nodes
KV cache defragmenter runs incrementally without causing GC spikes or CPU starvations (validated by flame graphs)
All changes covered by integration tests and a canary rollout plan; feature flags to toggle compacting allocator and defragmenter independently
notes: Spike completed week of 2026-02-17: three primary sources of fragmentation identified — legacy batcher arenas, per-request temp slices, and long-lived KV slab mismatches
Preferred compacting allocator: prototype uses jemalloc arena tuning + small object pooling; we evaluated a lightweight in-process compactor instead of full replacement to limit risk
KV defragmenter design: incremental slab walker that compacts under-utilized slabs per shard, backpressure-aware (sleeps when scheduler backlog or GPU utilization > 80%)
Scheduler handoff: add a short-lived handoff window during compaction so hot request lanes are migrated to warm slots avoiding preemption stalls
Dependency upgrade: bump jemalloc 5.x -> 6.2 in a separate subtask; this ticket includes preparatory API isolation and tests to make that upgrade low-risk
implementation_plan: Phase A (spike): run heap profiler on production-like load to catalog allocation sites and their lifetimes
Phase B (refactor): add allocator abstraction layer + migrate batcher ephemeral allocations to pooled region
Phase C (kvcache): implement incremental slab defragmenter as a background worker per-shard with tunable rate limits
Phase D (scheduler): add cooperative handoff and priority hinting so compaction work yields to latency-sensitive requests
Phase E (testing & rollout): integration tests, canary on dedicated capacity pool, staged ramp, observe telemetry for 72h before global rollout

risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Compactor interacts poorly with scheduler and increases tail latency -> Mitigation: progressive canary with feature-flag and runtime backpressure thresholds
Risk: Jemalloc upgrade exposes behavior changes -> Mitigation: keep allocator abstraction so jemalloc upgrade is toggled behind a flag and run regression suite
Risk: CPU steal during defragmentation -> Mitigation: defrag worker uses cgroups-friendly niceness and halts when CPU or GPU utilization exceeds configured threshold
